    Diagnose · start here · Steps 02 03 05 06

    Control Map DiagnosticKnow what runs, and what to keep.

    One bounded piece of work, mapped: roles, tools, triggers, exceptions and the AI already in use. Allowed and excluded sources, who decides, and the safest next step.

    1. Reading the current workCRM · ERP · email
    2. Keeping what worksSales confirms custom prices by phone
    3. Marking the sourcesCRM and ERP in · personal inboxes out
    4. Naming who decidesFinance approves credit, not a tool
    5. Choosing the next stepProceed · shrink · park · stop

    Not It does not build the system or run the workflow. No proof of savings or conformity.

    Request a call Service page

    Build · Steps 04 05 06 (+02 when needed)

    Digital Operations FoundationPut the work in order before AI.

    We put one slice of your operations in order: documents, requests, knowledge and data become clean records with a source, an owner and a baseline. On that base we can fine-tune your own AI model, running locally on your servers.

    Intake · Requests · Knowledge · Reconcile · Evidence · Your own model

    Not Not a system replacement. Your data trains only your own model, with your approval.

    Request a call All services

    Control · Steps 03 06 (+08 09 when needed)

    Agent Operations Safety AuditWhat can your agents really do?

    Every agent, tool and system it reaches, sorted into read, draft, prepared change and outside action. Checked in the system itself, not in the prompt, with logs, escalation, rollback and a shut-off plan.

    Agent actions · permission classesSynthetic example
    • Read records in the CRMAllowed · logged
    • Draft a replyAllowed · reviewed
    • Send to a customerNeeds approval · owner(needs a person)
    • Change a credit limitNot allowed(no)

    Shut-off Access can be removed; changes roll back.

    Not No security certificate, no production approval, no round-the-clock response.

    Request a call Service page

    Control · Steps 03 06 (+08 09 when needed)

    AI Governance Starter KitRules a team can follow.

    When AI use spreads faster than the rules: allowed, review-first and not-allowed classes, named roles, a data boundary, a check on public claims, and a review rhythm.

    Risk classes · who decidesSynthetic example
    • Summarise internal notesAllowed
    • Text a customer will readReview first · owner(needs a person)
    • Customer data in public toolsNot allowed(no)

    Review Every quarter, by the named AI owner.

    Not No legal advice, no conformity finding, no certification.

    Request a call Service page

    People · Steps 03 06 (+09 when needed)

    AI Literacy TrainingLearn it on your own work.

    For a founder, a manager, a team or a department: exercises on real workflows, which data may be used, how to check an output, when to escalate. A 30-day practice plan follows.

    Learning plan · by roleSynthetic example
    1. SalesDrafting offers, with reviewdone
    2. 2FinanceChecking output against the sourcein practicewaiting
    3. 3ManagersApproving and escalatingnext
    4. 4EveryoneFirst safe use by day 30next

    Not Not a generic prompt course, not a certificate.

    Request a call Service page

    Build · Steps 08 (+07 when needed)

    Controlled Workflow PilotRehearse it, then run it with a way back.

    One workflow, one main output. Scope and forbidden actions frozen, a baseline and a test set agreed, a rehearsal on synthetic cases, and only then a limited real run the client approves.

    Pilot · Order → InvoiceSynthetic example
    1. Charter and frozen scopedone
    2. Rehearsal on synthetic casesnormal · exception · blocked · reviewstep 07done
    3. 3Limited real runneeds approvalwaiting
    4. 4Result against the baselinenext
    5. 5Continue, revise or stopnext

    Not Buying a diagnostic does not authorise a pilot. A rehearsal is not live proof.

    Request a call Service page

    Review · Steps 09

    Fractional AI Operations PartnerSomeone keeps the map current.

    Only when an accepted map, audit or pilot shows a recurring need: a monthly review of access, agent permissions, exceptions and pilot metrics against the accepted baseline.

    Monthly reviewSynthetic example
    • Map and access updatedDone
    • Agent permission changeNeeds approval(needs a person)
    • Open exceptions2 open(needs a person)
    • Next periodOne priority

    Not Not a default subscription, not round-the-clock support, not outsourced IT.

    Specialist · Steps 04 05 06 (+09 when needed)

    DPP Readiness ReviewKnow your product data before a platform.

    Product, batch, material, supplier and lifecycle fields, each tied to its evidence source. Gaps and stale data show with their owner; carbon stays a question for the right expert to decide.

    Field readiness · one productSynthetic example
    • Material compositionSupplier declaration
    • Batch and lotERP
    • Recycled contentGap · supplier(no)
    • Carbon footprintQuestion · method(needs a person)

    Not Not an official product passport, no regulatory decision, no carbon credits.

    Specialist · Steps 06

    Tokenization Readiness ReviewMost answers need no token.

    What a token would represent, who holds which right, and what happens on transfer, revision or dispute. A database, a signed document, an audit log or a timestamp are checked first.

    Token fit · alternatives firstSynthetic example
    1. Database with access controldone
    2. Signed documentdone
    3. Audit logEnough for this casedecisiondone
    4. 4TokenOnly if still needednext

    Not No token issuance, no wallets or custody, no legal classification.
